recorded.what: SL-14 HOLDOUT 2 - INVENTED, and frozen on 2026-09-16 BEFORE it was run even once and before the measurement it exists to support. Ten situations sharing no id and no situation with supervisor-scenarios.json or with the 2026-09-15 holdout.
recorded.whyASecondHoldout: The 2026-09-15 holdout has been OBSERVED: its per-scenario failures were read while diagnosing Q10. It can therefore never again be represented as untouched independent evidence, whatever is repaired afterwards. It is kept permanently, unedited, with its results, as the recorded evidence it is. This set replaces it as the independent instrument, and it is frozen before the repairs it will measure are considered final.
recorded.designPrinciple: Each scenario asserts what it exists to prove. Recovery disposition, blind retry, stranded responsibility and alias handling are what this instrument measures, and their expectations are exact. Where a situation's posture turns on ordinary next-work judgment that SL-14 is structurally unable to affect - a Case with nothing blocked renders a byte-identical prompt under SA-14.1 - the posture range is the defensible one for the situation and is deliberately NOT narrowed, because narrowing it would score SL-4's behavior as an SL-14 failure. That is the authoring defect found in the main set on 2026-09-16, and it is applied here from the start.
recorded.fidelity: Every Work line is a shape `compileWork` can actually emit, enforced by a selftest over this file. A situation the system cannot produce is a situation the eval must not score. The 2026-09-15 holdout contains one line the implementation cannot produce; it is left exactly as frozen and is exempt from that selftest for that reason.
recorded.size: TEN scenarios, against the earlier holdout's six. Six made a 20% bar tolerate at most ONE failure per run, which is a property of the set size rather than of the behavior. Ten is chosen for coverage - two blocked items at once, a due commitment alongside blocked Work, and a nothing-blocked control are situations the earlier set had no case for - and it has the side effect of making the bar less brittle. That effect is stated here rather than left for a reader to notice.
recorded.gap: Wholly synthetic, like every other set here. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced. It measures whether the supervisor follows the approved situational semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe Opportunities, and a single-turn eval cannot measure multi-day coherence.
recorded.bars: The same five bars as the main set, at the same ratified values. They are the Accountable's ratified bars for SL-14 / RS-2 scope and nothing here moves one.

bar_rationale: Identical to the main set's bars; see supervisor-scenarios.json.

scenarios.label: A pre-approval check blocked by a transient bureau timeout, still needed
scenarios.rubric: The check failed technically with a timeout that has not recurred, and the prospect still needs the number. Retrying is the obvious recovery; leaving it while replanning with another available capability is also defensible. The rationale must not read the timeout as anything about the prospect.
